# DOC_GOVERNANCE — how to keep the documentation aligned (generated by virgilio init)

> **Why this exists**: discipline alone, across multi-session/multi-agent work, **drifts**. This doc
> consolidates the rules in one place and makes them **enforced** wherever possible (`virgilio check`).
> The governance in prose describes the REAL gate — if you touch the gate, update this doc.

## 0. Golden rule
Documentation is part of the **Definition of Done**, not an afterthought. A change isn't "done" until
the relevant doc is updated **in the same step as the code**. **A status flip is part of the task**: if
you close a phase, updating its `doc-status` is inside the task, not "to do later".

## 1. Entry chain (a new session reads in this order)
1. `CLAUDE.md` — onboarding + architecture + the Roadmap section with the current version status (CI-enforced `doc-status` line).
2. `DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md` → «Current Status» + Handoff log — where we are *right now* (**internal, git-ignored**: exists only in local checkouts; never link it from tracked docs — it 404s on GitHub).
3. `CHANGELOG.md` — what shipped, per release (historical, append-only).

## 2. SSOT map — a fact lives in ONE doc only; everything else LINKS to it
The root cause of drift is **duplication**. Every fact has **one owner**; elsewhere, a link, never a
copy.

| Fact | Owner | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Version number | `pyproject.toml` (synced to `app/__init__.py`, `app/core/config.py`, `manifest.json`, `CLAUDE.md` header by `scripts/bump_version.sh`) | bump script |
| Test-file counts | `CLAUDE.md` (markers `fact:unit-test-files` / `fact:integration-test-files`) | `virgilio check` (counts) |
| Current release status | `CLAUDE.md` (`doc-status` line + «Roadmap» section) — mirrored in the internal `DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md` «Current Status» | `virgilio check` (doc-status, on CLAUDE.md) + §9 audit |
| Release notes | `CHANGELOG.md` | historical, append-only |
| MCP tool count (20) | `CLAUDE.md` «Available Tools» table | **§9 audit only** (tool files ≠ `@mcp.tool` registrations: not cleanly countable from the filesystem) |

If you're about to write a number/status that **already exists** somewhere else: stop, link the owner
instead.

## 3. Automatic enforcement — `virgilio check`
A gate (`node virgilio/bin/cli.mjs check --config virgilio.config.json`, CI job `docs-gate`) checks
**doc declarations** against **REALITY** (filesystem + git-ref), not against more prose. Classes:
counts (marker vs. reality) · fact-dedup (SSOT) · banned phrases (reality-coupled: stale
`google-genai>=1.x`, removed `deep-research-pro-preview`) · internal links · doc-status (closed <!-- virgilio:allow-status-mention (the rulebook cites the banned phrases) -->
vocabulary). Config: `virgilio.config.json`. **Historical zones** (`CHANGELOG.md`, README «Changelog»,
roadmap «Version History» + Handoff log) are exempt from staleness; lines carrying
`virgilio:allow-status-mention` or `~~struck-through~~` are ignored (so the rulebook that cites the
banned phrases doesn't auto-fail). Before every commit that touches a doc/plan: `virgilio check` must
be green.

## 4. Absolute honesty (vocabulary)
- Never "done" without green-test evidence → otherwise **PARTIAL**/**SKIP**.
- Release status: `tagged` / `pypi-published` / `dxt-attached`. Never "released" without the tag on
  `origin/main` and the CI run green — the PyPI/`.dxt` reality is **external tier** (no probe adapter
  configured): if you can't verify it, write "not verifiable", never "verified".
- If something was skipped/bypassed/e2e-only → say so explicitly.

## 5. Handoff contract (before you stop)
Paste at the top of the **Handoff log** (in the internal `DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md`, append-only): *Done ·
Verified (how/where) · Deviations · Phase status · Next step · Links.* Update «Current Status» (and
`CLAUDE.md`'s `doc-status` date) if the overall status changed.

## 6. Superseded content — banner **then** archive
First, a `🔄 SUPERSEDED/HISTORICAL` banner linking to the current source; then, if the content is
prescriptive, move it under the historical zones (README «Changelog», roadmap «Version History»),
leaving a heading+stub+pointer behind.

## 7. Freshness
Every domain doc carries "**Updated YYYY-MM-DD** — what changed" (convention). Plan/status docs
**also** carry the machine-readable `doc-status` line (CI-enforced on `CLAUDE.md`; by convention on the
internal `DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md`). Don't mass-backdate unverified docs (a false attestation).

## 8. Checklist (end of every task)
- [ ] The relevant doc updated **in the same step as the code**.
- [ ] No count/status **duplicated** (the SSOT owner is linked instead).
- [ ] `virgilio check` **green** (+ `bite` green if you touched a rule).
- [ ] Honest status (tagged/pypi-published; PASS/PARTIAL/SKIP).
- [ ] Handoff + «Current Status» updated.
- [ ] Status flip for a closed phase = done (not "later").
- [ ] Found a false claim → added the mechanical rule that would have caught it (if clean).

## 9. Recurring semantic audit (end of milestone) — see `virgilio/modes/audit.md`
The gate covers the **known** classes; new ones emerge from a periodic audit that checks the docs
against **REALITY** (git log, the tags on `origin/main`, the PyPI release), not against other docs.
3 axes: (a) status vs. commits; (b) plans vs. real releases; (c) cross-doc consistency. Standing §9
items for this repo: the MCP tool count (20), the roadmap «Planned» sections vs. shipped versions,
PyPI/`.dxt` publication vs. "released" claims. Every clean false claim → a new rule; log the handoff
even at 0 findings.

> **Proxy-drift**: a green `virgilio check` is a **proxy** for the goal (honest docs), not the goal
> itself — it only says no KNOWN class has fired. The audit §9 against reality is the antidote, and
> it's **not replaceable by adding more checks**.
